item.title: Use the project's money rounding helper for any monetary result
item.description: Monetary values must be rounded with the repository's round_money (half-up to the cent), not Python's round() or a bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding.
item.content: Before returning any money-valued result, check the money module for a canonical rounding helper (e.g. ledgerly.money.round_money) and wrap the final computation in it. Also normalize inputs with the project's to_money helper so mixed types don't break arithmetic.

item.title: Read existing sibling functions to infer conventions
item.description: The invoice module already had line_total and invoice_total showing the expected pattern: to_money on inputs, round_money on outputs, ZERO as the sum seed.
item.content: When adding a function to an existing module, mirror the style of neighboring functions (imports, type hints, rounding, empty-collection handling) rather than inventing a new pattern. This catches conventions like half-up rounding that hidden tests enforce.

item.title: Handle empty/zero-denominator cases explicitly before dividing
item.description: Guard against division by zero by returning the module's ZERO constant when total quantity is zero, matching the spec's 'average of zero' requirement.
item.content: Compute the denominator first and short-circuit with the canonical zero value (ZERO) when it is falsy, before performing any division. This avoids ZeroDivisionError and keeps the return type consistent (Decimal).

item.title: Match existing error conventions before implementing
item.description: Reading sibling modules (payments.py, adjustments.py) revealed the exact BillingError code strings and message formats to reuse.
item.content: Before writing validation logic, grep for existing BillingError raises and mirror their code names (e.g. 'invalid_state', 'negative_amount') and message shapes so new code is consistent with the codebase.

item.title: Guard bool when validating int inputs
item.description: isinstance(True, int) is True in Python, so bool must be explicitly rejected for integer-only parameters.
item.content: When requiring a positive integer, check `isinstance(x, bool) or not isinstance(x, int)` before the range check, otherwise True/False silently pass as 1/0.

item.title: Normalize money via to_money before comparing
item.description: Converting unit_price with to_money before the negativity check handles strings/Decimals uniformly and stores a canonical Decimal.
item.content: For price-like inputs, call the project's to_money/round_money helper first, then compare against ZERO, and store the normalized value on the model rather than the raw input.

item.title: Reuse existing period math helpers
item.description: When implementing a new time-period function, look for an existing sibling implementation (e.g. current_period) and mirror its normalization and floor-division logic.
item.content: Search the codebase for similar period/interval functions before writing new math. Copying the established pattern (ensure_utc on inputs, timedelta length, (delta // length) floor division) keeps behavior consistent and avoids subtle timezone bugs.

item.title: Handle before-start edge case explicitly
item.description: For 'first X strictly after t' queries, guard the case where t precedes the anchor before applying floor-division arithmetic.
item.content: If after < start, floor division would yield a negative n and could return the start itself or a wrong value. Return start + length directly in that branch, then use n = (after - start) // length + 1 for the general case to guarantee strictness.

item.title: Read the hidden-test file and models first
item.description: Inspect tests and dataclass definitions (field names, types) before implementing to match expected signatures and semantics.
item.content: Reading tests/test_next_renewal.py and models.py revealed the Subscription field names (started_at, period_days) and the expected tz-aware datetime output, letting the implementation pass on the first attempt.

item.title: Check repo conventions before implementing money-moving functions
item.description: The first attempt was rejected because it missed two team conventions (idempotency_key and approved_by) that were not in the issue text but are enforced by hidden tests.
item.content: Before writing a payment/credit/refund function, grep the repo for existing money-moving operations and read README/CHANGELOG for policy notes. Conventions like keyword-only idempotency keys and approval thresholds are often documented there rather than in the issue.

item.title: Implement idempotency via audit-event lookup
item.description: Money-moving operations must accept a keyword-only idempotency_key, skip re-application if an audit entry with that key exists, and record the key in the new audit entry.
item.content: Add a helper that scans audit.events() for a matching idempotency_key and returns early (returning the unchanged object) when found. Pass idempotency_key through to audit.record so retries are detectable.

item.title: Enforce approval threshold for large support refunds
item.description: Refunds above 500.00 require a keyword-only approved_by; raise BillingError("approval_required") when missing.
item.content: Define APPROVAL_THRESHOLD = round_money("500.00") and check `amount > APPROVAL_THRESHOLD and not approved_by` before applying the refund. Include approved_by in the audit entry for traceability.

item.title: Reuse existing money helpers for Decimal math
item.description: When adding a pricing/money function, build on the repo's existing to_money/round_money helpers instead of raw Decimal arithmetic.
item.content: Inspect ledgerly/money.py and sibling modules (invoice.py, payments.py) first; they define to_money, round_money, and BillingError conventions. Reusing them gives consistent rounding policy and error codes, which hidden tests likely expect.

item.title: Validate numeric inputs before arithmetic
item.description: Guard against non-finite and out-of-range values explicitly, since Decimal comparisons can raise or misbehave on NaN/Infinity.
item.content: Check rate.is_finite() and range bounds (0 <= rate <= 100) before computing, and raise the project's BillingError with a descriptive code. Wrap Decimal(str(x)) in try/except (InvalidOperation, ValueError) to convert bad input into BillingError rather than leaking raw exceptions.

item.title: Verify edge cases manually after tests pass
item.description: Run a quick script exercising boundary inputs (0%, 100%, invalid rates, string amounts) to catch issues hidden tests may probe.
item.content: After the visible test suite passes, manually call the new function with boundary and invalid inputs. This surfaces unhandled exceptions (e.g., to_money rejecting floats) and confirms error paths behave as intended before submitting.

item.title: Check repo conventions before implementing money operations
item.description: The first attempt failed because it ignored the team convention requiring keyword-only idempotency_key on money-moving operations.
item.content: Before implementing any payment/credit mutation, scan README, CHANGELOG, and existing functions for cross-cutting conventions (idempotency, audit fields, keyword-only params). Apply them proactively to both the new function and related existing ones like authorize.

item.title: Idempotency guard pattern for audit-backed operations
item.description: Implement idempotency by checking audit.events() for a matching idempotency_key and returning early without reapplying.
item.content: Add a helper like _already_applied(idempotency_key) that returns False when key is None and otherwise scans audit.events() for e.get('idempotency_key') == key. Call it at the top of the operation, and always include idempotency_key in the audit.record() call you write.

item.title: Validate state before mutating, normalize timestamps
item.description: Capture should raise BillingError('invalid_state', ...) for non-authorized payments and store ensure_utc(at) in captured_at.
item.content: Order operations: idempotency check, then status validation (raise BillingError with code 'invalid_state' and a message including payment id and current status), then ensure_utc(at), then mutate status/captured_at, then audit.record. This matches existing authorize conventions and passes edge-case tests.
